instructions.name: claim_jackpot
docs: Pays the committed jackpot to the snapshot-proven winner of the jackpot
target interval. One claim; never falls back to any other escrow.

instructions.name: claim_round_reward
docs: ET-only in-epoch reward. Proportional to stake on the winning tile;
bounded by the pool bonus cap; never touches PT or any custody asset.

instructions.name: commit_jackpot
docs: Commits the current jackpot vault balance for this epoch's draw. The
cohort is the committed prize snapshot; nothing about eligibility can
change after this. Unclaimed jackpots roll over by simply remaining in
the vault — expiry moves no funds.

instructions.name: create_pool
docs: Creates one isolated pool instance: immutable accepted asset identity,
receipt mints, and the three segregated vaults.

accounts.name: accepted_mint
docs: Any SPL/Token-2022 mint may be recorded at pool creation; asset
selection is a policy decision enforced at the authority, and the
identity below is immutable afterwards.

instructions.name: expire_jackpot
docs: Unclaimed jackpots move no funds: the balance simply remains in the
vault and rolls into a future epoch's commit. Accepts COMMITTED so a
never-fulfilled jackpot draw cannot block rollover either.

instructions.name: expire_unclaimed_prize
docs: Expiry also cancels a stuck randomness request (requested but never
fulfilled): without this a stalled authority could block rollover for
the pool forever. A late fulfillment is rejected by the status change.

instructions.name: fulfill_jackpot_with_vrf
docs: Permissionless jackpot draw from the ORAO VRF (see
`fulfill_round_with_vrf` for the trust model).

accounts.name: orao_network_state
docs: program (both constraints below); no caller-supplied network state
can stand in, even one that ORAO genuinely owns.

accounts.name: orao_request
docs: the handler verifies the exact derivation; bytes are parsed by

instructions.name: fulfill_prize_with_vrf
docs: Permissionless prize draw from the ORAO VRF (see
`fulfill_round_with_vrf` for the trust model).

instructions.name: fulfill_round_with_vrf
docs: Permissionless round settle from the ORAO VRF (pull model). Anyone may
submit once the oracle network has fulfilled the request bound to this
round's stored seed; the winning tile derives from oracle-signed
randomness, never from the submitter.

instructions.name: fund_jackpot
docs: Sponsor/operations jackpot funding. The only inflow to the jackpot
vault; no instruction can route principal or prize assets here.

instructions.name: fund_prize
docs: Sponsor/operations prize funding. The only inflow to the prize vault.

instructions.name: initialize
docs: Program-global initialization. Requires the deployed program's upgrade
authority so the first caller cannot seize the protocol (finding I-01).

instructions.name: refresh_entries
docs: Deliberately allowed while paused: refreshing entries only restores the
documented matched-withdrawal route (PRD principle 6). It moves no
custody asset and creates no new exposure.

instructions.name: set_pause
docs: Guardian pause is per pool. Refresh and withdrawal stay live by design.

instructions.name: withdraw
docs: Withdrawal is never blocked by pause, epoch state, or rollover.

types.name: Epoch
docs: One epoch's schedule is fully committed at creation and has no edit path.
Ordering is enforced at creation: starts_at < entry_cutoff_at <= ends_at
<= prize_snapshot_at <= claim_deadline, within the pool's duration bounds.

fields.name: jackpot_status
docs: 0 = no jackpot this epoch; see JACKPOT_* states.

fields.name: vrf_randomness_state
docs: ORAO VRF network-state account, or zero to run mock-only.

types.name: Pool
docs: One isolated pool instance. The accepted asset, its token program, the
receipt mints, and all vault identities are set here exactly once, at
creation, and have no update path. Limits are equally immutable in v1
(a timelocked `set_pool_limits` is a documented future upgrade).

fields.name: latest_epoch_id
docs: Set to the newest epoch when it is created; used to prove a supplied
epoch account is the active one rather than a stale open epoch.

types.name: ProtocolConfig
docs: Program-global roles and mode. Holds no custody and no asset identity.

fields.name: vrf_randomness_state
docs: ORAO VRF network-state account; zero disables `*_with_vrf` settle
(mock-only deployments). Mock fulfillment additionally requires
`production_mode == false`, so a VRF-configured production pool can
never fall back to the operator-supplied path.

fields.name: seed
docs: Final VRF seed: the requester's client seed mixed with the slot hash
of the request slot, so it is unknowable before the request lands.
